sections.h2: What closing costs does a North Carolina seller actually pay?
sections.html:
A North Carolina seller pays the deed excise tax, the cost of paying off any existing loan, a closing attorney, and the recording charge for any paper the seller must file. The exact total depends on the contract, so the settlement statement from the closing attorney is the document to check line by line.

Some charges are fixed by statute and some are negotiated in the sales contract. This page sticks to the ones the General Statutes spell out, because those do not change from one closing table to the next.

  • The excise tax on the deed, which the law puts on the seller.
  • The payoff of the mortgage or deed of trust, plus the work needed to get that lien cleared from the record.
  • Attorney fees for the person who handles the deed and the title review.
  • Recording fees at the register of deeds for any document the seller has to file.
  • The county property tax bill for the year, which has its own due date and interest schedule.

Commission, repair credits and similar items come from the contract, not the statutes. Ask the listing agent or closing attorney to put every one of them in writing before you sign.

sections.h2: Why does a North Carolina home sale need an attorney?
sections.html:
North Carolina treats deed preparation as the practice of law, so a licensed attorney has to prepare the deed and pass on the title. G.S. 84-2.1 lists deeds, mortgages and the abstracting or passing upon of titles among the acts that count.

The same statute lets a real estate broker fill in a preprinted form, and it lets any person or website complete a preprinted residential lease. It then adds that nobody without a law license may prepare a contract or deed that conveys an interest in North Carolina real property for a third person. In practice that is why a North Carolina closing runs through a law office instead of an escrow company.

For a seller, this means you should pick or at least approve the closing attorney early. The attorney will review the chain of title, collect the payoff figure, prepare the deed and make sure the excise tax and recording fee reach the register of deeds. If you are selling for cash to a buyer who names the attorney, you can still ask for a copy of the draft settlement statement before closing day.

sections.h2: How does the excise tax fit into a seller's closing costs?
sections.html:
The seller owes it. G.S. 105-228.30 sets the rate at one dollar for each five hundred dollars of the consideration or value of the interest conveyed, counting any fractional part, and says the transferor pays the register of deeds before the deed is recorded.

Because the tax rides on the price, it is usually the largest single line the statutes assign to a seller. The closing attorney normally takes it out of your proceeds and hands it to the register of deeds with the deed. The statute also covers a parcel that sits in more than one county: the tax goes to the county that holds the greater value of the land.

Half of what the register collects stays with the county general fund. The other half, less refunds and the county allowance, goes to the state Department of Revenue each month. Our North Carolina excise tax page walks through who is exempt and how the fractional-part rule works.

sections.h2: Which recording fees does the register of deeds charge?
sections.html:
The register of deeds charges a fee set by G.S. 161-10, and the same schedule applies in every county. Fees are collected before a document is filed, and the statute calls them complete and exclusive.

Document or serviceFee as the statute prints it
General instrument, first 15 pages$26.00, plus $4.00 for each added page
Deed of trust or mortgage, first 35 pages$64.00, plus $4.00 for each added page
Satisfaction or cancellation of a deed of trust or mortgageNo fee
Plat$21.00 per sheet
Certified copy$5.00 first page, $2.00 each added page
Nonstandard document$25.00 added charge
Extra instruments inside one document$10.00 each

Source: G.S. 161-10, North Carolina General Assembly. A seller's deed is a general instrument. The deed of trust line belongs to the buyer's lender, so it does not usually appear on the seller's side of the statement.

sections.h2: What happens to my mortgage payoff and the recorded lien?
sections.html:
Your lender has to send a satisfaction for recording within 30 days after it receives full payment. G.S. 45-36.9 sets that clock, and recording the satisfaction costs nothing at the register of deeds.

If the lender misses the deadline, it owes you actual damages. After the period ends you can also send a written demand by a method that gives proof of receipt. If the lender still has not filed within 30 days of receiving that demand, the statute adds one thousand dollars plus reasonable attorney fees and court costs. That right belongs to the landowner who sent the demand and cannot be assigned.

If the loan was a line of credit or secured future advances, full payment is not enough by itself. The creditor must also receive a request to close the line or a similar notice. Ask your closing attorney to include that request with the payoff letter so the lien does not linger on the record after the sale.

sections.h2: When does a deed take effect against other buyers and lenders?
sections.html:
A deed does not protect the buyer against lien creditors or other purchasers until it is registered in the county where the land sits. G.S. 47-18 says that rule covers conveyances, contracts to convey, options, leases over three years, and rights of first refusal or first offer.

Priority follows the order and time of registration. That explains why the closing attorney records the deed the same day funds move, and why the excise tax has to be paid first: the register of deeds will not accept the deed without it. As a seller, you want the recording confirmation in hand before you consider the sale complete.

  • Ask when the deed will be recorded and by whom.
  • Ask for the book and page or document number once it posts.
  • Keep the recorded satisfaction of your old loan with your closing papers.

sections.h2: How do property taxes show up at a North Carolina closing?
sections.html:
North Carolina county property taxes are due and payable September 1 of the fiscal year and can be paid at face amount through the first days of January. Under G.S. 105-360, payments made on or after January 6 pick up interest at two percent, and from February 1 interest runs at three-fourths of one percent for each month or fraction until the bill is paid.

The tax lien does not wait for the bill to arrive. Under G.S. 105-355 the lien on a parcel attaches as of the listing date set by G.S. 105-285, with penalties, interest and costs attaching at the same time. That makes the property tax status one of the first things a title review checks.

How the year's bill is split between buyer and seller is a contract term. Ask the county tax office for the current bill and payment status, and ask the closing attorney how the contract divides it before you rely on any estimate.

sections.h2: What should I ask my closing attorney before signing?
sections.html:
Ask for a written list of every charge that will come out of your proceeds and the source of each. A short conversation before closing day catches most surprises.

  • What rate and base is the excise tax figured on, and which county receives it?
  • What is the payoff figure, and will the lender's satisfaction be tracked and recorded within the 30-day window?
  • Which recording fees fall on the seller and which on the buyer?
  • How does the contract split the current property tax bill?
  • When will the deed record, and will you send the recording information?

If you are comparing a traditional listing with a direct cash sale, run the same checklist on both. The statutory items above do not change with the type of buyer, so the real difference shows up in the contract terms.

faqs.q: Who pays the excise tax when I sell a house in North Carolina?
faqs.a: The seller does. G.S. 105-228.30 puts the duty on the transferor, who pays the register of deeds before the deed can be recorded. The closing attorney usually deducts it from your proceeds.

faqs.q: Do I have to hire a lawyer to sell my house in North Carolina?
faqs.a: In practice yes, because preparing a deed and passing on title count as practicing law under G.S. 84-2.1. A broker may fill in a preprinted form, but nobody without a law license may prepare the deed or contract for someone else.

faqs.q: Does it cost anything to record the release of my old mortgage?
faqs.a: No. G.S. 161-10 lists no fee for recording a satisfaction or cancellation of a deed of trust or mortgage. Your lender must submit the satisfaction within 30 days after payoff under G.S. 45-36.9.

faqs.q: What are the register of deeds fees for a regular deed?
faqs.a: A general instrument is $26.00 for the first 15 pages and $4.00 for each added page under G.S. 161-10. A deed of trust or mortgage is $64.00 for the first 35 pages plus $4.00 for each added page. Ask your register of deeds if a nonstandard document charge applies.

faqs.q: Which county gets the excise tax if my land is in two counties?
faqs.a: The tax is paid in the county that holds the greater value of the land, according to G.S. 105-228.30. Ask the closing attorney to confirm which register of deeds will receive the deed.
